rules.statement: When a change alters a symbol, contract, behavior or semantic, update every place that references it (callers, sibling implementations, tests, XML docs, README and design docs) so they stay consistent with the change.
rules.why: Out-of-sync references leave a change inconsistently delivered and docs or tests contradicting the code.
rules.check: For each changed member, option, error code or behavior in the diff, look for other references to it in the touched files and nearby code, tests and docs, and flag any that still describe or assume the old behavior.

rules.statement: When two code paths are meant to behave the same way (parallel paths, sibling modules, symmetric operations such as read/write or encode/decode), report any asymmetry between them, such as validation, error handling, logging or edge-case handling present in one but missing from the other.
rules.why: Asymmetry between things meant to be equivalent is a gap that leaves the capability inconsistently delivered.
rules.check: Compare the changed path with its sibling or counterpart line by line for argument validation, failure modes, logging/telemetry and edge cases. Flag whatever one has and the other lacks without a stated reason.

rules.statement: Trace each capability a change is meant to deliver down to its low-level implementation, and report a missing failure mode, edge case, invariant, validation or logging path as an in-scope gap even when the ticket didn't call out that detail.
rules.why: Closing such a gap completes the existing capability rather than adding new functionality, so it belongs in the change.
rules.check: For each intended capability, check that the implementation handles invalid input, empty/null/boundary values, failure of dependencies and invariant violations, and that failures are logged or observable. Flag any path that silently does the wrong thing or is unhandled.

rules.statement: Don't report missing brand-new functionality beyond the change's intended scope, and don't flag existing extra functionality that isn't part of the intended scope; limit gap findings to the behavior the change is meant to deliver.
rules.why: The review completes the intended capability. Asking for new features or removal of unrelated existing ones is out of scope.
rules.check: Before raising a 'missing feature' finding, confirm that it is a low-level part of a capability the change, ticket or spec actually intends, not a new capability.

rules.statement: When a spec, design doc, ticket or README describes the intended behavior, use it as the source of intent and report places where the implementation or its tests fall short of or contradict that documented behavior.
rules.why: The documented intent is how low-level gaps against the intended behavior are found.
rules.check: Read the referenced spec, design doc or README section and compare each stated behavior, requirement and error case with the code and tests in the diff. Flag requirements that are unimplemented, implemented differently or untested.

rules.statement: Report duplicated logic introduced or touched by a change that can drift out of sync, and contradictions or unclear semantics and naming between the touched files.
rules.why: Duplicated or contradictory logic and unclear semantics cause inconsistencies when only one copy is later changed.
rules.check: Look for the same computation, validation or mapping repeated across touched files, names that mean different things in different places, and members whose behavior doesn't match their name or docs.
